meta.task: Add end-to-end tests to an existing web app
meta.title: Add E2E Tests to an Existing Web App
meta.promptIntro: Add end-to-end tests to this existing web app, covering the flows that matter most. Take the suite the whole way: a test plan mapped from the app itself, specs that run green locally and in CI with the flakes chased down rather than waited out, and a human review before the suite gates a merge.

nodes.label: Gather app details & critical flows
nodes.description: Ask the user which flows matter most (login, signup, checkout...), how the app is started locally, which framework they prefer (Playwright, Cypress), whether test accounts and seed data exist, and which CI provider merges gate on. Several rounds of back-and-forth before anything can start.

nodes.label: Spelunk the repo for the user flows
nodes.description: Read package.json, the router, and page components by hand to trace each critical journey screen by screen. No sitemap, no docs — just the repo and a growing scratch file.

nodes.label: Write the test plan by hand
nodes.description: Turn the spelunking into a plan: URLs, form fields, and expected outcomes per flow, written down before any framework is installed.

nodes.label: Install & configure test framework
nodes.description: Pick the framework that fits the stack, npm install it, download browser binaries, generate the config file (baseURL, timeouts, retries, screenshot-on-failure), and add npm scripts so the suite is runnable.

nodes.label: Boot the app & babysit the dev server
nodes.description: Start the dev server and database, seed test data, create throwaway test users, wait on ports, and keep the server alive between runs. Every new session repeats this ritual; a crashed server mid-suite means starting over and re-seeding.

nodes.label: Hunt stable selectors in the DOM
nodes.description: Load each page and inspect the rendered DOM by hand to find selectors that will survive a re-render. Most classes are hashed or utility soup, so this usually means editing the app's own components to sprinkle data-testid attributes — a change per element, per page.

nodes.label: Write a spec per critical flow
nodes.description: For each flow in the test plan: script the navigation, fill the forms, click through, assert the outcome. Heavy copy-paste of setup/teardown boilerplate between specs, adjusted slightly each time; auth state and fixtures re-plumbed per spec.

nodes.label: Run the full suite headless
nodes.description: Run every spec against the local server and watch the output scroll by. Each full pass takes minutes; nothing else can safely touch the app state while it runs.

nodes.label: Suite green?
nodes.description: Read the run summary: all specs passing, or are there failures — and are the failures real bugs, broken selectors, or intermittent flakes?

nodes.label: Re-run specs to reproduce the flake
nodes.description: Run the failing spec over and over until the intermittent failure shows itself again — minutes per attempt, with no guarantee it fires this time.

nodes.label: Compare failure screenshots by hand
nodes.description: Put the failure screenshot beside the live page and hunt for what differed: a spinner, a late render, an animation caught mid-frame.

nodes.label: Swap selectors & tune explicit waits
nodes.description: Swap the brittle selector, add a wait, tune its timeout, and hope — the cycle that burns a whole session across editor, terminal, and browser.

nodes.label: Wire the suite into CI
nodes.description: Author the CI workflow YAML by hand: install dependencies and browser binaries, cache them, boot the app inside the CI job, run the suite, and upload traces and screenshots as artifacts on failure. YAML indentation and CI-specific env vars invite silent mistakes.

nodes.label: Push & wait — CI green?
nodes.description: Push the branch and wait out each CI run — minutes per attempt, refreshing the web UI and reading raw logs. Green on the CI machine, or a failure that never happens locally: headless-only timing, slower hardware, cold caches, missing env vars?

nodes.label: Human review of specs & CI setup
nodes.description: A teammate reviews the specs, the data-testid changes to app code, and the CI workflow before anything merges. Wait for the review, answer questions, and address requested changes — the merge is gated on their approval, not on green checks alone.

nodes.label: Merged e2e suite running in CI
nodes.description: The e2e suite is merged and runs on every push: critical flows covered, failures block the merge, traces and screenshots attached to every red run.

edges.label: CI-only flake: headless timing, slower machine
changes requested: more coverage, tighter asserts

suggestions.name: safishamsi/graphify
suggestions.claim: Turns a codebase into a queryable knowledge graph so agents reason over structure instead of grepping.
suggestions.promptFragment: Learn the app under test with safishamsi/graphify before any framework is set up: query its knowledge graph for the routes, pages, and components behind each critical flow instead of reading the router and page files by hand. Draft the test plan straight from what the queries return.

replaceWith.label: Query the app's structure for the plan
replaceWith.description: graphify answers the routes, screens, and components per flow in one query — the test plan falls out of the answer.

suggestions.name: obra/superpowers
suggestions.claim: A full engineering methodology (brainstorm→plan→TDD→review) that turns one-shot vibe coding into disciplined shipping.
suggestions.promptFragment: Write the specs under obra/superpowers once the selectors are in hand: work its disciplined loop — one flow, one spec, run it, prove it — instead of scripting every flow in one pass and untangling the pile of failures afterwards. Let its review step read the suite before CI ever sees it.

replaceWith.label: Specs via superpowers' TDD loop
replaceWith.description: One spec at a time, run and proven as it lands — boilerplate and guessed-at cases stop piling up between specs.

newEdges.label: changes requested: more coverage, tighter asserts

suggestions.name: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
suggestions.claim: Gives Claude live eyes on a real browser — debugging, performance traces, and page inspection in one MCP.
suggestions.install: claude mcp add chrome-devtools -- npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest
suggestions.promptFragment: When a spec fails or flakes, debug it with ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp instead of re-running blind and comparing failure screenshots by hand: drive the page it failed on, watch the console and network live, and inspect the DOM the selector actually missed. Fix the selector or the wait against what the live page shows, then re-run.

replaceWith.label: Debug the flake on the live page
replaceWith.description: chrome-devtools-mcp drives the failing page with console, network, and DOM in view — the fix comes from evidence, not reruns.
